The term "Tadris" refers to a teacher or a scholar, symbolizing the importance of passing down knowledge from one generation to another.

In Islamic tradition, knowledge is considered a gateway to gaining closeness to Allah (swt). Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) once said, "Seeking knowledge is an obligation on every Muslim," emphasizing the spiritual importance of education.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Rushd, also known as Averroes, wrote a major commentary on Aristotle's 'Nicomachean Ethics' titled 'Tadhjim al-Maslul ila Maqasid al-Shar'iyyah' or 'The Decisive Treatise on the Intentions of the Practical Sciences'. This work had a significant influence on European scholastic philosophy and ethics. It was written between 1175 and 1198 CE.
historical_references.context: Ibn Rushd's commentary on Aristotle's 'Nicomachean Ethics' was a major contribution to medieval philosophical thought and had a significant impact on European scholastic philosophy and ethics.

historical_references.reference: Al-Jahiz, a prominent Arab scholar during the Abbasid Caliphate, wrote a comprehensive encyclopedia on natural history and zoology titled 'Kitab Al-Hayawan' or 'Book of Animals'. He used the term 'Tadhrib' in the title of the first volume of this work, which means 'instruction' or 'education'. This work is considered one of the most important contributions to Arabic and Islamic literature on natural history and zoology.
historical_references.context: Al-Jahiz's 'Kitab Al-Hayawan' is an important work in Arabic and Islamic literature on natural history and zoology. The term 'Tadhrib' in the title of the first volume refers to the educational aspect of the work.
